newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Duma to return to anti-Yeltsin move in Feb. [CORRECTED 16:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russia Duma to return to anti-Yeltsin move in Feb. [CORRECTED 16:25 GMT]

text.p: The Russian parliament's press service said the State Duma agreed on Wednesday to postpone a final vote on a motion to remove President Boris Yeltsin on health grounds until February, giving time for more discussion.

(Corrects earlier report in which Reuters erroneously claimed that the Duma had voted to reject the motion. But a Duma spokesman said the chamber had voted against holding an immediate final vote and would review the resolution in February.)

A Duma spokesman told reporters the chamber voted by 102 to 87 to reject a move to vote immediately on the resolution, which the chamber had earlier adopted "in principle". Pro-government deputy speaker Alexander Shokhin had earlier said the second vote was a rejection of the anti-Yeltsin resolution itself.
The chamber voted 229 to 63 for the motion "in principle". The motion said Yeltsin's term should be declared over because he was too sick and called for new presidential elections.

The resolution's sponsor, communist Viktor Ilyukhin, then called for deputies to be given time to discuss the move in their constituencies and come back for a "definitive" vote in February. A liberal deputy urged the house to vote right away.
Shokhin, chairing a debate boycotted by many Yeltsin supporters, responded to the latter proposal and called on the confused and rowdy chamber to vote immediately.

After this second vote, Shokhin told reporters that deputies had finally rejected Ilyukhin's resolution. But the Duma press service later said that the chamber had simply rejected a motion on an immediate vote and would return to the debate next month.
